meta.title: CAPLE C2 — Portuguese
meta.subtitle: 700 words · European Portuguese · both directions
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck, as two cards per word: Portuguese → English (see the Portuguese, recall the meaning) and English → Portuguese (see an English meaning, recall the Portuguese). 700 words for level C2 of the Common European Framework, which is the level of DUPLE, the exam awarded by CAPLE — the Centro de Avaliação de Português Língua Estrangeira at the Universidade de Lisboa. None of them appears in the A1, A2, B1, B2 or C1 deck, so the six together come to 5,100 words. THIS DECK TEACHES EUROPEAN PORTUGUESE. CAPLE sets its exams on the European standard, so the train is o comboio and the bus o autocarro; the mood is the conjuntivo and not the subjuntivo; and the first person plural of the preterite is falámos, not falamos. That choice reaches into every part of the deck rather than sitting in this description: the frequency ordering is taken from the European half of the subtitle corpus and not the Brazilian one, Wiktionary's Brazil-marked verb forms and word senses are excluded, and example sentences carrying a Brazilian marker are rejected. Where the reference inventory gives both a European and a Brazilian word for the same thing — it writes them together, as uma chávena/xícara de — the deck teaches the European one. There is no published CAPLE word list — the exam board publishes exam specifications and no vocabulary inventory — so the words are taken from the reference description CAPLE's own resources page points at: the Referencial Camões PLE, the Instituto Camões' level-by-level account of Portuguese, whose C2 inventory of Noções is read for the topical vocabulary and whose Funções and Gramática sections supply the greetings, the courtesy formulas and the closed classes that a list of notions names without ever writing out. Only the inventory of words is taken; none of the Referencial's own prose appears in this deck. The cards are ordered roughly by how common the word is in everyday European Portuguese, so the words you will meet most often come first: the order comes from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles, with a reflexive verb placed by the verb it is formed from. Every noun carries its article, so the gender is learnt with the word (376 of them), and its plural sits directly beneath it; the article is coloured for its gender. A noun or adjective with a distinct feminine is taught as a pair rather than as two words (110 of them): o professor, a professora above os professores, as professoras. Each of the 139 verbs carries its full conjugation — the non-finite forms, all six simple tenses of the indicative, the three of the conjuntivo, both imperatives, and the personal infinitive, which is the one tense Portuguese has that no other Romance language does. Six persons are shown, from eu to eles; você and vocês are named on the third-person rows, which is where they take their verb and the single most confusing thing about the Portuguese verb for a beginner. The 9 reflexive verbs are conjugated the European way, with the pronoun after the verb rather than in front of it, including the first person plural that drops its -s before -nos and the future and conditional, where the pronoun goes inside the verb. The pronoun is picked out in colour so its three positions can be seen at a glance; in ordinary writing it is joined to the verb with hyphens, as chamo-me, levanta-te, chamamo-nos and chamar-me-ei. Real example sentences come with 407 of the 700 words, three apiece for 231 of them and one or two for the rest; the sentence corpus has nothing at all for the remaining 293, which are kept because the word list is set by the reference inventory and not by the corpus, chosen where possible to show three different inflected forms rather than the same one three times, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside it. Tatoeba's Portuguese is overwhelmingly Brazilian, so sentences carrying a Brazilian marker are rejected outright; what remains is mostly variety-neutral rather than positively European, which is a limit of the corpus and not something the filter can repair. Word list: Referencial Camões PLE (instituto-camoes.pt). Meanings, genders, plurals and conjugations: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency ordering: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.

fields.Examples:
Por quê ainda todo mundo está de pé?
Why's everyone still standing?
Eu não vou dizer às senhoras por quê.
I won't tell you why.
O quê?! Você comeu meu urso de chocolate?!
What?! You ate my chocolate bear?!

fields.English:
interjection
thank you (said by a woman)
fields.Examples:
A senhora não é obrigada a fazer isso.
You don't have to do that.
As senhoras são obrigadas a fazer isso?
Are you obliged to do that?
Ela disse que foi obrigada a fazer isso.
She said she had to do that.

Querido, você vai fazer as compras por mim?
Honey, will you go shopping for me?
Olha, querida, você não pode fazer isso.
Look, honey. You can't do that!
Eles dois eram tão queridos!
They were both so cute!

cards.question: o coração
cards.answer: heart (organ of the body); sweetheart (term of endearment)
cards.answerText: heart (organ of the body); sweetheart (term of endearment)

fields.English:
noun, masculine
  • heart (organ of the body)
  • sweetheart (term of endearment)
fields.Examples:
Acalma-te de bater, ó meu coração!
Calm down your beating, oh, my heart!
Podemos dormir esta noite com os corações leves, Caroline!
We may sleep tonight with light hearts, Caroline!
A mãe de Tom ficou de coração partido.
Tom's mother was heartbroken.

fields.Portuguese: o rei, a rainha
fields.English:
noun, masculine and feminine
king (male monarch)
fields.Forms: pluralos reis, as rainhas
fields.Examples:
A filha de um rei é uma princesa.
A king's daughter is a princess.
A águia é a rainha das aves.
The eagle is king of birds.
O ouro é o rei dos reis.
Gold is the king of kings.

cards.question: o olho
cards.answer: eye; a hole in cheese; bread or similar items
cards.answerText: eye; a hole in cheese; bread or similar items

fields.English:
noun, masculine
  • eye
  • a hole in cheese
  • bread or similar items
fields.Examples:
Os olhos deles estão a brilhar de alegria.
Their eyes are glittering with joy.
Alguma coisa aconteceu com o meu olho direito.
Something has happened to my right eye.
Feche os seus olhos e diga-me o que ouve.
Close your eyes and tell me what you hear.

O Tom passou a noite toda no bar.
Tom spent all night at the bar.
Ela é muito jovem para ir a bares.
She is too young to go to bars.
Tom comprou bebidas para todo mundo do bar.
Tom bought drinks for everybody in the bar.

O diabo vem me ver todas as noites.
The devil comes to see me every night.
O que diabos há de errado com você?
What the hell is wrong with you?
Essa criança é um diabinho.
That kid is a little demon.

fields.English:
adjective
apposed (placed next or near to)
fields.Examples:
Eu aposto que o Tom estava com fome.
I bet Tom was hungry.
Se importa em fazer uma aposta?
Care to make a wager?
Não gosto de fazer apostas.
I don't like to make bets.

Quando o juiz fala, todos no tribunal ouvem.
When the judge speaks, everyone in the courtroom listens.
Os cidadãos recorrem aos tribunais em busca de justiça.
The citizens go to court for justice.
Você já foi testemunha num caso de tribunal?
Have you ever been a witness in a court case?

Por um acaso você sabe onde ela mora?
Do you happen to know where she lives?
Por acaso você tem alguma fotografia de Tom?
Do you happen to have any photographs of Tom?
Por acaso você sabe a data do exame?
Do you happen to know the date of the exam?

Desculpe-me. Gostaria de apontar três erros no artigo acima.

He lives above me.

cards.answerText: pit; hole (hollow spot in a surface); burrow (a tunnel or hole dug by a creature)

  • pit
  • hole (hollow spot in a surface)
  • burrow (a tunnel or hole dug by a creature)
fields.Examples:

Esta janela é à prova de bala.
This window is bulletproof.
A polícia vai fazer você encontrar as balas.
The police will get you to find the bullets.
Três dos cadáveres tinham marcas de bala.
Three of the bodies had gunshot wounds.

Tom wasn't sitting beside Mary.
Tom viu Mary sentada ao lado de John.

Ficamos sentados juntos, em silêncio, durante algum tempo.
We sat together in silence for some time.

fields.English:
noun, feminine
loss (instance of losing something)
fields.Examples:

It's a waste of time and money.
Quem vai compensar as perdas?
Who will compensate for the loss?
Isso é uma perda de tempo e dinheiro.
That's a waste of time and money.

Isso não é legal; é chato.
This isn't fun. This is boring.
É por isto que não podemos ter coisas legais.
This is why we can't have nice things.
É raro conhecer pessoas legais como você.
It's rare to meet nice people like you.

Algures num futuro distante, um cérebro diabólico planeou a escravização da humanidade.
Somewhere in the far future a diabolical brain plotted the enslavement of mankind.

fields.English:
noun, masculine
  • creed
  • credo (a religious belief system)
fields.Examples:

fields.English:
adverb

fields.Examples:

Tom definitely won't do that anymore.
Eu definitivamente não vou fazer isso de novo.
I definitely won't do that again.

cards.question: disposto, disposta
cards.answer: willing (prepared and wanting to do something); feeling all right; not indisposed
cards.answerText: willing (prepared and wanting to do something); feeling all right; not indisposed

fields.English:
adjective
  • willing (prepared and wanting to do something)
  • feeling all right
  • not indisposed
fields.Examples:
O Tom não estava disposto a fazer isso.
Tom was unwilling to do that.
Mary disse que estaria disposta a nos ajudar.
Mary said she'd be willing to help us.
O que você e Tom estão dispostos a fazer?
What are you and Tom up to?

A população mundial tem tendência a aumentar.
The world's population tends to increase.
O Japão faz parte das potências econômicas mundiais.
Japan ranks among the economic powers of the world.
Dia 11 de julho é o Dia Mundial da População.
July 11 is World Population Day.

O Tom disse-me que não estava chateado.
Tom told me he wasn't angry.
Ela disse-me que estava chateada.
She told me she was upset.
Nós estamos chateados.
We're upset.

Eu canto desde os seis anos de idade.
I've been singing since I was six.
Seu pai gravou alguns cantos de pássaros para ele.
His father recorded some birdsong for him.
O homem no canto dirigiu-se ao marido.
The man in the corner addressed himself to the husband.

O Tom foi gentil, mas a Mary não.
Tom was kind, but Mary wasn't.
Agradeço muito à senhora as palavras tão gentis.
I appreciate your kind words.
Ela tem sido muito gentil com a gente.
She's been really kind to us.

Esta é a primeira vez que eu fumo.
This is the first time I've smoked.
A partir de hoje não fumo mais.
From now on, I won't smoke anymore.
Eu queria poder acabar com o vício do fumo.
I wish I could break the habit of smoking.
